data.claim: `ddflow bug fixed <lint-bug> --lint-exempt <reason> --landed <sha>` is refused because `--landed` is placed in `_close_lint_exempt`'s `takes_no` set, which refuses any non-empty entry.
data.falsifier: The command would return exit 0 (recording the landing) instead of exit 3 if `--landed` were not in the disallowed set.
data.mechanism: `bug_close.bug_fixed` builds `takes_no = {"--landed": landed, ...}` and passes its non-empty entries to `_close_lint_exempt`, which returns a refusal naming each disallowed flag. `--landed` names the commit reference, not the waived regression test.

chunk_findings.detail: The new implementation assumes both `cfg.enforce` and `cfg.enforce.machine_local_keys` are present and iterable. The previous code deliberately treated a missing `enforce` section or a `machine_local_keys` value of `None` as “no extra keys” by returning `set()`. For a config-like object where `[enforce]` is absent or represented as `None` (for example a partially constructed config or a test double such as `types.SimpleNamespace(enforce=None)`), `_extra_keys` now raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'machine_local_keys'` instead of returning an empty set; if `machine_local_keys` itself is `None`, it raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. This can crash config/setup paths that previously handled missing optional enforce settings gracefully.

chunk_findings.detail: For the exact regression input `FINDING MEDIUM y.py:1`, the new fallback makes `detail` equal to the location string (`"y.py:1"`), while `title` is also the location. That only changes an empty body into a bare coordinate; it still gives triage no proposition to refute or confirm, so the bug’s stated symptom (a finding cannot be answered with a probe) remains. chunk_findings.detail: The change only defines the new table scanner; nothing in the shown change calls `_scan_task_tables` or adds it to the existing `scan_todos` path (the manifest is `+109 -0` and the diff contains no invocation). As written, the production import path still uses the old table parsing, so the reported `SX-seed` title/glob corruption remains. A regression test that imports `_scan_task_tables` directly can pass while the actual bug is still present.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_scan_task_tables

chunk_findings.detail: `_table_task` indexes `tbl` with the header column indices without checking that the data row actually has that many cells. A valid GFM table may omit trailing empty cells, so for header `| id | title | needs | globs |` and data row `| T-1 | Foo | Bar |` (missing the globs cell), `_table_cells` returns only three cells while `table_cols["globs"]` is `3`, causing an `IndexError` during import. The same applies to a row missing a `needs` cell.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_table_task

chunk_findings.detail: `_table_row` treats any table-like row containing an exact `id` or `title` cell as a new header row, not as data. For example, after header `| id | title |`, a data row `| T-1 | id |` is classified as a header with `{"id": 1}`; the row is not imported, and subsequent rows are parsed with the wrong column mapping, silently dropping tasks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_table_row

chunk_findings.detail: For the exact repro input `FINDING MEDIUM y.py:1` (with `STATUS: FINDINGS 1`), the new fallback sets `detail` to the same string as `title` and `location`. The bug’s stated failure is not merely that the body string is empty, but that a location-only finding cannot be refuted or confirmed with a probe because triage has no proposition to answer. Substituting the missing paragraph with the coordinate leaves triage with only `y.py:1`: there is still no reviewer claim to refute or confirm. The regression test only asserts `detail == "y.py:1"`, a truthy digest, and failed outcome, so it passes with this unactionable text; the earlier probe likewise only proves non-emptiness, not answerability, so the previous finding still holds.
